steps.title: Construct the dependency frontier
steps.purpose: Locate the target’s remaining proof obligations.
steps.input: Target acceptance conditions; recursive dependency graph
steps.procedure: The native producer is unresolved. The linked cartographer prescribes classifying missing premises, bridge objects, route lemmas and proof debt, while checking cycles.
steps.criterion: A dependency must support the target logically; similarity or a mentioned lemma does not discharge it.
steps.output: Intended frontier: open uniform-gap proof obligation
steps.failure_next: Disposition assessment requires this frontier; the signature does not establish that cartography was performed.
steps.example: Separate the available conditional decay theorem from the unproved assertion that every graph has gap at least the same c greater than zero.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Select a justified obligation
steps.purpose: Select work that controls target completion.
steps.procedure: Assess which open node controls the target and distinguish work readiness from release readiness or stall.
steps.criterion: An open necessary premise prevents treating the target as complete.
steps.output: Work disposition: common-gap task and justification
steps.failure_next: Original policy routes onward; the native return neither proves the premise nor executes that route.
steps.example: Because uniform decay depends on the open common-gap premise, select that premise for investigation rather than re-deriving the conditional theorem.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: The target is a diffusion bound uniform across a graph family. A conditional decay theorem is available, but its common spectral-gap premise is open.
workflows.contrast: If the common-gap premise is discharged for the target family, navigation should reassess the remaining acceptance obligations. It must not continue selecting the same already closed gap merely because its node is prominent.

steps.title: Bound the search
steps.purpose: Bound admissible evidence and comparisons.
steps.input: Sensor context; measurement constraints; calibration target
steps.procedure: Separate available evidence from desired measurements and delimit the regime in which candidate explanations must operate.
steps.criterion: A useful scope retains the target and exposes missing controls.
steps.output: Bounded sensor record and admissible comparisons
steps.failure_next: Both formation branches consume this scope; insufficient controls constrain subsequent conclusions.
steps.example: Freeze the measured offset, temperature and elapsed-time columns; note that no intervention has yet separated thermal and temporal effects.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Propose a mechanism
steps.purpose: Propose mechanisms with distinguishable predictions.
steps.input: Bounded sensor record, shared with pattern induction
steps.procedure: Construct rival dependencies and specify the observable on which they could disagree, rather than naming a cause without a test.
steps.criterion: A candidate must address the calibration target and admit a falsifier.
steps.output: Candidate thermal mechanism; clock-drift rival
steps.failure_next: Both probes receive the hypothesis with the pattern; unsupported mechanisms remain candidates.
steps.example: Thermal sensitivity predicts offset changes with temperature at fixed elapsed time; clock drift predicts changes with elapsed time at fixed temperature.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Extract the observed regularity
steps.purpose: Describe observed variation without inferring causation.
steps.procedure: Compare offsets across the observed conditions and state the trend together with its observational limits.
steps.criterion: The pattern must be supported within the record and retain confounding.
steps.output: Provisional offset trend, with confounding retained
steps.failure_next: Join this pattern with the hypothesis for both probes; it is not independent confirmation.
steps.example: The record shows increasing offset while both temperature and time increase. This trend fits both candidate mechanisms and selects neither.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Derive model predictions
steps.purpose: Derive comparable predictions under explicit assumptions.
steps.procedure: Specify variables, controls and measurement assumptions; preregister which outcomes favor, weaken or fail to distinguish each rival, including an inconclusive region, before deriving comparable predictions.
steps.criterion: Predictions must concern the same observable and regime as the target.
steps.output: Conditional thermal and temporal model predictions
steps.failure_next: Refutation later receives these implications with the contrast assessment; model failure remains informative.
steps.example: Under thermal sensitivity, holding temperature fixed removes the predicted thermal offset change; under clock drift the offset can still grow with time.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Design the discriminating contrast
steps.purpose: Identify a control that separates the rivals.
steps.input: Discovery hypothesis + pattern, shared with model probe
steps.procedure: Perturb one relevant assumption or control while preserving the others; explain which dependency the contrast tests.
steps.criterion: A contrast is discriminating only if rivals predict different outcomes under justified controls.
steps.output: Contrast assessment: informative control or non-identifiability
steps.failure_next: Send this assessment to refutation; unavailable controls require a new measurement plan.
steps.example: Compare readings at fixed temperature but different elapsed times. Continued drift challenges a purely thermal account if other conditions remain stable.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Combine the challenges
steps.purpose: Locate what survives both challenges.
steps.input: Model implications + contrast assessment; scoped assumptions
steps.procedure: Compare predicted differences with the available contrast and localize inconsistency; do not count two analyses of one record as two independent experiments.
steps.criterion: A negative verdict needs a particular violated prediction, not an unfavorable label.
steps.output: Refutation assessment: proposed falsifier, no observed refutation
steps.failure_next: Calibration receives this finding with the original hypothesis and pattern.
steps.example: If a future fixed-temperature test finds drift, it would defeat the thermal-only prediction under its control assumptions. The current confounded record supplies no such finding.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Allocate the next discovery action
steps.purpose: Choose continuation, reorientation or reset.
steps.input: Hypothesis + pattern + refutation; retained calibration target
steps.procedure: Compare target relevance and what the next action could change; preserve alternatives that remain indistinguishable.
steps.criterion: Continuation needs new learning or a sharper test, not repeated failure.
steps.output: Routing assessment: remaining mechanism question and justification
steps.failure_next: Original cross-cycle routing is a policy; the native return does not execute a marathon.
steps.example: Retain the trend and both rival explanations; request the fixed-temperature measurement. Demote thermal-only only if the predicted falsifier is subsequently observed under the stated controls.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: A constructed sensor record contains temperature, elapsed time and a drifting offset. Thermal sensitivity and clock drift are rival explanations.
workflows.contrast: If temperature and elapsed time are perfectly confounded, neither probe identifies the cause. The proper next action is a discriminating measurement, not promotion of the more elaborate explanation.

steps.title: Repair the missing premise
steps.purpose: Identify a premise sufficient for uniform decay.
steps.input: Active obligation: decay uniform in graph size
steps.procedure: First attempt deduction; locate the absent support, propose small competing premise sets, and attach a falsifier to each.
steps.criterion: Compare explanatory coverage and compatibility without treating simplicity as proof.
steps.output: Route hypothesis: positive common spectral gap
steps.failure_next: Send this conjectural premise to derivation; incompatible premise sets require revision.
steps.example: The gap becomes the proposal that every graph in the selected family has first positive eigenvalue at least a common c greater than zero.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Expose the conditional consequence
steps.purpose: Derive the proposed premise’s conditional payoff.
steps.procedure: Derive what the added premise would imply while tracking where it is used; do not discharge that premise by using it.
steps.criterion: A valid conditional derivation must retain the norm, subspace and common constant.
steps.output: Exponential-decay claim, conditional on the gap
steps.failure_next: Refutation receives this claim; a missing spectral lemma remains an obligation.
steps.example: The proposed gap yields mean-zero norm decay bounded by the initial norm times exp(-ct), conditional on the symmetric Laplacian assumptions.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Attack the exact strengthening
steps.purpose: Test the strengthening without conflating premise and consequence.
steps.input: Derived decay claim; retained uniform-gap premise
steps.procedure: Probe boundary families and seek a counterexample to the implication actually being asserted; distinguish a false premise from an invalid derivation.
steps.criterion: A counterexample must satisfy the stated domain and attack the same quantifier.
steps.output: Refutation finding: connectedness insufficient for a common gap
steps.failure_next: Pass the targeted finding to calibration; bounded non-refutation supplies no missing proof.
steps.example: For cycle graphs the first positive eigenvalue is 2-2 cos(2 pi/n), which tends to zero. This defeats a size-independent gap for all connected graphs.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Choose the next proof task
steps.purpose: Choose a sharper task from the localized failure.
steps.input: Original derived claim + its refutation assessment
steps.procedure: Compare the route with the target and identify whether a premise, graph family or bound must change.
steps.criterion: Continuation must sharpen the obligation; repeating the same failed premise is not progress.
steps.output: Routing assessment: bounded reframing or retargeting rationale
steps.failure_next: Original policy can route onward or stop; the native sequence returns an assessment only.
steps.example: Retain the conditional decay theorem and replace the unrestricted family claim by the task of finding structural assumptions that imply a uniform gap.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: Follow a proposed uniform diffusion bound for du/dt=-Lu over finite connected undirected graphs, using the symmetric combinatorial Laplacian L and mean-zero initial data.
workflows.contrast: If the input instead supplies a proved common spectral-gap bound for a restricted family, the cycle objection no longer defeats that premise. The conditional decay implication can then support work on that family; connectedness alone cannot.

steps.title: Locate the representational obstruction
steps.purpose: Distinguish conceptual obstruction from unfinished calculation.
steps.procedure: Trace the failed implication to the role played by the carrier, invariant or equivalence relation.
steps.criterion: An obstruction diagnosis must explain why existing objects fail at the named boundary.
steps.output: Obstruction diagnosis: representative-dependent convergence criterion
steps.failure_next: Mediation consumes this diagnosis; a merely missing calculation should remain a derivation task.
steps.example: Two gauge-equivalent representatives can be far apart in the chosen norm, so representative convergence need not express physical-state convergence.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Propose the mediating object
steps.purpose: Propose a carrier for the intended question.
steps.procedure: Propose a quotient or other mediator, naming what it would preserve and its first possible failure regime.
steps.criterion: The desired convergence theorem cannot be hidden inside the mediator's definition.
steps.output: Mediation hypothesis: gauge-equivalence classes
steps.failure_next: Transfer must turn this proposal into specified maps; a name alone is insufficient.
steps.example: Replace the proposed carrier of raw representatives by classes under gauge equivalence, while leaving existence of suitable dynamics as an obligation.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Specify the bridge
steps.purpose: Specify the mediator’s maps and compatibility burden.
steps.procedure: Specify projection from representatives to classes and the compatibility needed for dynamics to descend.
steps.criterion: Equivalent representatives must induce the same class evolution for the bridge to be well defined.
steps.output: Projection bridge; open dynamics-compatibility obligation
steps.failure_next: Deduction uses this bridge conditionally; an absent compatibility law blocks unconditional transport.
steps.example: For representative evolution F, require the class of F(x) to equal the class of F(y) whenever x and y are gauge equivalent.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Derive a bridge consequence
steps.purpose: State the bridge’s conditional consequence.
steps.procedure: Formulate the transported statement on the new carrier and retain each bridge premise.
steps.criterion: The consequence must concern equivalence classes without silently restoring representative identity.
steps.output: Class-level evolution or convergence claim, conditional on its premises
steps.failure_next: Refutation tests this consequence; convergence estimates remain separate from well-definedness.
steps.example: A quotient trajectory can be defined from F only if changing the representative leaves its next class unchanged; convergence would then be a class-level question.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Test preservation
steps.purpose: Test whether the representation is well defined.
steps.procedure: Search for equivalent inputs whose evolved outputs cease to be equivalent; localize the precise preservation law at fault.
steps.criterion: A bridge fails this test when one physical input class receives two distinct output classes.
steps.output: Refutation assessment: well-definedness defect or bounded surviving claim
steps.failure_next: Pass the finding to routing with the retained bridge; no found defect is not a proof.
steps.example: Choose equivalent x and y with inequivalent F(x) and F(y). The proposed class dynamics is ambiguous, independently of any convergence estimate.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Route the conceptual repair
steps.purpose: Choose proof work or bridge reconstruction.
steps.procedure: Compare target contribution, validation strength and the exact preservation defect; distinguish an informative repair from a repeated blocked route.
steps.criterion: A work-ready bridge needs explicit obligations that address the bottleneck.
steps.output: Refinement assessment: compatibility-repair obligation
steps.failure_next: Original policy routes work or release and stops refutation; native routing is a returned value.
steps.example: Keep quotienting as a candidate representation but require a compatible evolution law; do not advertise the quotient name as a solved convergence problem.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: A state-convergence argument uses a norm that distinguishes gauge representatives even when they represent the same observable state.
workflows.contrast: If equivalent representatives evolve into equivalent classes, the proposed quotient passes this well-definedness test. Convergence still requires its own argument; compatibility alone does not establish it.

steps.title: Construct a bounded proposal
steps.purpose: Bound a release claim by accumulated support.
steps.input: Iteration evidence packet; target identity; support references
steps.procedure: The native construction is unresolved. The linked promoter prescribes separating robust support from fragile support and exposing target drift and missing machinery prerequisites.
steps.criterion: The proposed scope cannot exceed the regime actually supported by evidence.
steps.output: Intended proposal: supported finite estimate; unsupported continuum extension
steps.failure_next: Promotion assessment consumes the proposal; nominal run references do not enforce identity preservation.
steps.example: Write the finite-regulator estimate as supported within its assumptions and list continuum passage and uniform error control as open obligations.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Assess promotion or repair
steps.purpose: Assess promotion against the evidence boundary.
steps.procedure: Compare claim scope with missing construction and transfer objects; distinguish target repair, conceptual repair and rejection.
steps.criterion: Endpoint spectral machinery cannot replace an absent analytic transfer premise.
steps.output: Promotion disposition: bounded promotion or specified repair
steps.failure_next: Original policy may promote, route repair or stop; native output alone performs none of these effects.
steps.example: Restrict the release to the finite estimate or request the missing transfer object; do not accept the continuum announcement from the same packet.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: A release packet contains a finite-regulator correlation estimate but proposes a continuum conclusion without a same-theory transfer or uniform error bound.
workflows.contrast: Restricting the proposal to the evidenced finite-regulator result can make a bounded claim supportable. Adding more fixed-regulator examples cannot by itself repair the missing uniform transfer.

steps.title: Ground the route evidence
steps.purpose: Ground statements before proposing proof connections.
steps.procedure: Normalize theorem bodies and retain hypotheses, provenance and the status of each imported claim.
steps.criterion: Only licensed statements may serve as established premises; topic proximity is insufficient.
steps.output: Grounded definitions; proposed translation claims with status
steps.failure_next: Route formation consumes this evidence; ungrounded statements remain conjectural or excluded.
steps.example: Record the uniform lower-bound target, the central definition, and a translation candidate whose uniformity condition has not been checked.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Propose a useful connection
steps.purpose: Identify a target-relevant missing implication.
steps.procedure: Compare candidate reductions and cross-component links using symbol roles and method overlap, separating proposed edges from established dependencies.
steps.criterion: A route must supply proof relevance beyond graph centrality.
steps.output: Route hypothesis: candidate proof-to-circuit translation
steps.failure_next: Deduction exposes its consequence; the selected bridge is still hypothetical.
steps.example: Choose the less central translation because, if uniform, it could connect a proof lower bound to the circuit statement required by the target.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Expose the route's consequence
steps.purpose: Expose the candidate bridge’s mathematical payoff.
steps.procedure: Derive the proposed implication while tracking the target quantifier that the translation must preserve.
steps.criterion: Do not replace a uniform target with a nonuniform consequence.
steps.output: Translation consequence, conditional on required uniformity
steps.failure_next: Assessment checks this consequence's relevance and missing support.
steps.example: The route would transfer the chosen lower-bound obligation only if one uniform construction supplies the translated objects across input sizes.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Assess the consequence
steps.purpose: Identify the decisive gap in the payoff.
steps.procedure: Compare the consequence to the original target and inspect whether graph prominence concealed a missing theorem.
steps.criterion: A highly connected definition does not compensate for an unproved translation property.
steps.output: Consequence assessment: missing uniformity-preservation support
steps.failure_next: Entrypoint revision consumes this diagnosis instead of repeating the full ambitious target.
steps.example: The definition contributes vocabulary, but the route's progress depends on proving that translation does not use size-specific advice.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Revise the entrypoint
steps.purpose: Reduce the route to a testable obligation.
steps.procedure: Anchor an agenda on one statement, attach its hypotheses and links, and specify a stop or pruning condition.
steps.criterion: The entrypoint must directly control the missing implication.
steps.output: Entrypoint hypothesis: uniformity-preservation lemma
steps.failure_next: Refutation challenges this entrypoint before a proof handoff is justified.
steps.example: Replace the full lower-bound demand with the lemma that the proposed translation uses no nonuniform advice as input size varies.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Challenge the entrypoint
steps.purpose: Test the selected lemma in its stated regime.
steps.procedure: Search for a translation instance requiring advice or a regime change; distinguish an actual counterexample from a missing argument.
steps.criterion: A falsifier must attack the selected lemma, not a different complexity claim.
steps.output: Falsification finding: advice dependence or unresolved uniformity proof
steps.failure_next: Final readiness joins this finding with the same entrypoint.
steps.example: A translation that chooses unrelated advice at each input size defeats the proposed uniformity lemma, leaving any nonuniform statement separate.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Bound the proof handoff
steps.purpose: Assess a proof task with its criticism intact.
steps.procedure: Retain the route dossier, hub-bias diagnosis and transfer burden when judging readiness.
steps.criterion: Readiness cannot arise solely from connectivity or a favorable label.
steps.output: Readiness assessment: bounded proof task or reorientation rationale
steps.failure_next: Original routing needs a separate ProofQueueItem adapter; the native return does not construct it.
steps.example: Hand off a precise unresolved uniformity obligation if viable, or stop the advice-dependent route without claiming a lower bound.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: A lower-bound knowledge base contains a highly connected complexity-class definition and a less connected proposed proof-to-circuit translation. The target requires uniformity.
workflows.contrast: If the translation is independently shown to preserve uniformity, it can support a suitable proof entrypoint. Merely increasing the centrality of the definition never supplies that implication.

steps.title: Freeze the conceptual pressure
steps.purpose: Fix protected successes and the unresolved distinction.
steps.procedure: Separate target commitments from replaceable concepts and identify what a new bridge must explain.
steps.criterion: The frontier must retain regime limits and the successes a replacement may not discard.
steps.output: Bounded frontier: relation between descriptions; protected distinctions
steps.failure_next: Hypothesis formation consumes this frontier; ordinary missing calculation does not justify a new ontology.
steps.example: Record agreement on current observables, different state variables, and an open question about predictions beyond that observable set.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Invent alternatives
steps.purpose: Generate meaningfully different explanatory structures.
steps.procedure: The linked skill prescribes 8--12 isolated raw candidates, blinded reconstruction of at least six semantic families unless verifier-replayed constraint evidence justifies fewer, and six reflective transformations. Propose primitive, mediator or transport changes and candidate-specific falsifiers; this two-candidate example illustrates one distinction only.
steps.criterion: Semantic paraphrases do not create new families; each alternative must change a meaningful dependency.
steps.output: Candidate explanations: latent mediation or direct observable translation
steps.failure_next: Refutation examines candidate content; a nominal hypothesis port does not implement the larger portfolio procedure.
steps.example: A latent carrier attempts to explain both state descriptions, while direct translation relates selected observables without asserting a common underlying state space.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Challenge a candidate's distinctions
steps.purpose: Test what the proposed bridge fails to preserve.
steps.procedure: Identify a decisive observable, intervention or identity distinction and ask whether the proposal preserves it.
steps.criterion: A criticism must change a dependency or reveal an unmet prediction, not merely request different wording.
steps.output: Refutation finding: unresolved discrimination or specific candidate defect
steps.failure_next: Selection receives the original hypothesis with this finding, preserving its identity.
steps.example: Ask whether two states merged by the latent carrier could disagree on a newly measured observable. If so, that merging needs justification or repair.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Select without forcing consensus
steps.purpose: Select defensible content without forcing preference.
steps.procedure: The linked skill prescribes preregistered non-compensatory dimensions, at least three separately configured blinded judges and sham/rival controls. Compare complete candidates and retain a nondominated set; missing judges, warrants or failed controls yield a typed null rather than a forced preference.
steps.criterion: Failure on a required dimension cannot be offset by elegance elsewhere.
steps.output: Selected content; unresolved alternatives where warranted
steps.failure_next: Bridge revision consumes selected content; non-ready plural results have an original exploration route.
steps.example: Keep both latent mediation and direct translation if current evidence cannot distinguish them; make the missing observable test part of their retained burden.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Make a selected bridge explicit
steps.purpose: Specify a useful formal correspondence.
steps.input: Selected content; open identity and regime obligations
steps.procedure: Specify maps, carriers and preservation conditions only where formal representation adds a concrete obligation.
steps.criterion: Category or type language must expose a mediator or transport obstruction, not supply prestige.
steps.output: Revised bridge: specified compatibility obligation
steps.failure_next: Deduction uses this bridge; linked procedures make formal routes conditional although the native sequence is linear.
steps.example: For the direct-translation candidate, specify an observable map and demand agreement of predictions over the chosen regime, without assuming full state-space equivalence.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: State the exact formal burden
steps.purpose: Formulate the bridge’s precise proof obligation.
steps.procedure: Express the compatibility statement with explicit domain and quantifiers, retaining assumptions as premises.
steps.criterion: The claim must not strengthen regime-limited prediction agreement to unrestricted equivalence.
steps.output: Formal map-compatibility claim; retained premises and regime
steps.failure_next: Readiness assesses this statement; the act of stating it does not discharge it.
steps.example: The obligation becomes prediction preservation for the specified observable map on the bounded regime; unseen observables remain outside the claim.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Assess readiness for theorem work
steps.purpose: Assess proof readiness while retaining unresolved choices.
steps.procedure: Check that objects and the required implication are definite; distinguish readiness from an established theorem.
steps.criterion: An unresolved choice of carrier or target statement prevents an unconditional readiness judgment.
steps.output: Calibrated candidate: ready, non-ready or unresolved plural status
steps.failure_next: Original policy can send ready claims to theorem work; the native sequence supplies no switch.
steps.example: If the observable map and its regime are specified, queue its compatibility lemma; if the carrier remains ambiguous, return to conceptual selection.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: Two effective descriptions match existing measurements in a bounded regime but use different state variables. A latent carrier and a direct observable translation are candidate bridges.
workflows.contrast: If a new observable distinguishes the candidates, selection must incorporate that difference. Agreement on the original measurements alone warrants neither equivalence nor a unique winner.

steps.title: Construct the exact conditional theorem
steps.purpose: Derive the exact queued obligation.
steps.input: item.premises: queued exact_statement; connected-graph, subspace and gap premises
steps.procedure: Order lemmas without circular dependence and propagate constants, norms and quantifiers through each inference.
steps.criterion: Every inferential step must identify its premises and preserve the theorem's scope.
steps.output: Exact claim; retained premises and undischarged formal obligations
steps.failure_next: Refutation receives this claim; a missing lemma remains visible rather than silently closed.
steps.example: For du/dt=-Lu on the connected graph, expand the mean-zero vector in positive-eigenvalue modes. Each coefficient evolves by exp(-lambda t), giving Euclidean-norm decay at rate at least c.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Search for a defeater
steps.purpose: Challenge edge cases without weakening the claim.
steps.input: Exact claim; gap premise; open obligations
steps.procedure: Test small, degenerate and adversarial cases; classify a failed step as a false statement, wrong quantifier, model mismatch or missing technique.
steps.criterion: Favorable examples cannot substitute for a missing spectral argument.
steps.output: Refutation assessment: scoped surviving theorem or localized defect
steps.failure_next: Calibration retains this finding with the exact claim; repair must name any changed premise.
steps.example: The constant mode violates unrestricted decay but is excluded by the mean-zero premise. Without the gap premise, cycle families defeat a common positive rate.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Calibrate the proof disposition
steps.purpose: Distinguish proof discharge from conditional or blocked work.
steps.input: Exact theorem claim + its refutation assessment
steps.procedure: Check the lemma chain and retained obligations; issue a bounded disposition and failure certificate when a bridge remains missing.
steps.criterion: A proof gate cannot discharge an obligation merely because refutation found no counterexample.
steps.output: Claim; finding; proof gate; optional failure certificate
steps.failure_next: Original policy routes accepted work or failure; the native return is no terminal proof acceptance act.
steps.example: Accept only the explicitly justified conditional spectral estimate; if spectral decomposition has not been supplied, retain that proof debt in the disposition.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: Prove Euclidean-norm decay for the symmetric combinatorial Laplacian of a finite connected undirected graph on mean-zero initial data, assuming its first positive eigenvalue is at least c greater than zero.
workflows.contrast: If the queue requests all initial data, a nonzero constant vector defeats positive-rate decay. The theorem must retain the mean-zero restriction; an assessment of that restricted theorem cannot certify the broader one.

steps.title: Interpret a possible contribution
steps.purpose: Identify the bounded result’s scientific use.
steps.procedure: Propose the smallest standalone bridge, obstruction or reframing and identify who could use it.
steps.criterion: A contribution hypothesis must not inherit the breadth of the original unsolved target.
steps.output: Contribution hypothesis: obstruction to the insufficient premise
steps.failure_next: Refutation tests this interpretation, not merely the underlying calculation.
steps.example: Propose that the cycle example shows why connectedness is too weak for the intended uniform diffusion bound and motivates a stronger structural condition.

steps.title: Challenge support and significance
steps.purpose: Test contribution scope and novelty support.
steps.procedure: Test hidden premises, proxy drift and prior-art boundaries; compare what the result actually rules out.
steps.criterion: Neither one slow family nor a true calculation establishes a general impossibility of fast diffusion.
steps.output: Support assessment: bounded obstruction; unestablished breadth and novelty
steps.failure_next: Final readiness joins this finding with the same contribution hypothesis.
steps.example: Reject the claim that fast diffusion is impossible in general; retain only failure of connectedness to imply a uniform gap over the specified family.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Assess value and enablement
steps.purpose: Assess target value and communication readiness.
steps.procedure: Separate conceptual value, target alignment and actual downstream enablement; compare the prior missing condition with the next task's requirements.
steps.criterion: Exploration payoff cannot by itself establish paper readiness or novelty.
steps.output: Readiness record: useful obstruction; open merit burden
steps.failure_next: Original policy can route to elaboration or stop; returned audit components are not extra native occurrences.
steps.example: The result enables replacing an inadequate premise by a search for sufficient structural assumptions; any claim of publishable novelty still requires separate evidence.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: A completed cycle-graph example defeats a size-independent spectral gap from connectedness alone. The task is to identify what this negative result enables.
workflows.contrast: If the result merely restates a known example without a new warranted use, its mathematical validity does not establish novelty or publication merit. Enablement needs a specific downstream change.

steps.title: Recover the actual expansion need
steps.purpose: Distinguish mathematical gaps from prose gaps.
steps.procedure: Classify each request as a definition, coefficient, finite check, transfer theorem or explanatory paragraph and recover the smallest honest scope.
steps.criterion: Do not treat all expansion markers as requests to assert stronger results.
steps.output: Expansion scope: finite matrix certificate; separate application obligation
steps.failure_next: Extension formation consumes this scope; unresolved geometric work remains distinct.
steps.example: Specify the two-by-two symmetric matrix, the range absolute t at most one half, and the still-unproved geometric transfer estimate.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Propose a bounded extension
steps.purpose: Construct the missing finite certificate.
steps.input: Matrix scope; parameter range; missing sign certificate
steps.procedure: Define the carrier and entries, order coefficient extraction before the sign test, and state the lemma that will consume it.
steps.criterion: A finite extension must expose its quantitative range and avoid assuming the application.
steps.output: Extension hypothesis: exact eigenvalue-based positivity certificate
steps.failure_next: Refutation tests this proposed extension and its parameter boundary.
steps.example: For the matrix with diagonal 1 and off-diagonal t, propose eigenvalues 1+t and 1-t and hence a lower bound of one half on the stated range.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Test the extension's validity
steps.purpose: Test the finite result and its application boundary.
steps.input: Proposed matrix certificate; range; intended use
steps.procedure: Check the algebra and boundary values, seek a non-example, and localize any absent transfer lemma.
steps.criterion: Finite sign success does not discharge a geometric comparison hypothesis.
steps.output: Validity assessment: scoped matrix calculation; open transfer debt
steps.failure_next: Readiness joins this assessment with the same extension hypothesis.
steps.example: At t=1/2 the eigenvalues are 3/2 and 1/2; at t=2 they are 3 and -1. The range matters, and neither calculation supplies geometric transfer.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Integrate with its evidence boundary
steps.purpose: Assess inclusion while preserving proof obligations.
steps.procedure: Explain how the finite lemma fits the argument, retain the counterexample and separate paper readiness from unproved application claims.
steps.criterion: An integrated paragraph cannot turn a missing bridge into an accepted theorem.
steps.output: Finite certificate; expansion validation; readiness decision
steps.failure_next: Original proof-required routing needs a ProofQueueItem adapter; native return does not execute it.
steps.example: Add the exact finite positivity result and its range to the draft, while sending the geometric transfer estimate to further proof work instead of claiming the application.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: A finite-result draft requests a sign certificate for the matrix with diagonal entries 1 and off-diagonal entries t, for absolute t at most one half. A geometric application still needs a separate transfer estimate.
workflows.contrast: If t is allowed to exceed 1, the smaller eigenvalue becomes negative and the proposed positivity extension fails. If the finite range is retained, positivity still cannot establish the missing geometric transfer.

steps.title: Ground the reviewed state
steps.purpose: Ground criticism and repair in the same state.
steps.input: Evidence bundle; implemented argument; persisted claims
steps.procedure: Separate mathematical results, implementation behavior, assumptions and open obligations before interpreting progress.
steps.criterion: Disagreement about scope must remain explicit rather than averaged into confidence.
steps.output: Formalized review state: visible decay; unsupported global extension
steps.failure_next: Both parallel branches consume this same state; their coexistence gives no independence guarantee.
steps.example: Write the state as a valid-looking visible-sector calculation plus the additional, unsupported claim that every physical excitation is gapped.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Localize the defeater
steps.purpose: Locate the unsupported implication.
steps.input: Grounded review state, shared with repair formation
steps.procedure: Challenge quantifiers and representation coverage, separating a defect in the inference from a defect in implementation.
steps.criterion: A useful diagnosis names the missing burden and the claim it affects.
steps.output: Defeater assessment: missing observable-density premise
steps.failure_next: The join later compares this finding with repairs; the repair branch does not consume it directly.
steps.example: An abstract direct-sum spectral countermodel preserves the reported correlations while adding energies approaching zero. It defeats the unrestricted correlation-to-gap inference and identifies the missing completeness premise; it is not a constructed Yang--Mills theory.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Propose recovery options
steps.purpose: Propose repairs that preserve useful content.
steps.input: Formalized review state; no parallel refutation output
steps.procedure: Propose a changed representation, missing bridge or narrower claim, explaining what each option would preserve.
steps.criterion: A repair proposal must alter the defective dependency rather than relabel the current result.
steps.output: Repair alternatives: richer observables or sectorial theorem
steps.failure_next: Final calibration must test these options against the separately produced defeater.
steps.example: From the visible/global mismatch, propose either constructing a dense observable-generated subspace or explicitly restricting the conclusion to the visible sector.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Judge repairs against criticism
steps.purpose: Match repairs to diagnosed defects.
steps.procedure: Check which proposal addresses the missing implication and record whether understanding sharpened, stalled or regressed.
steps.criterion: A proposed repair does not resolve a defect merely by appearing in the same packet.
steps.output: Reorientation assessment: repair assignment or conceptual reorientation
steps.failure_next: Original policy routes assignments; native return does not execute repair or prove density.
steps.example: The narrower claim resolves the overstatement; the richer observable construction remains a research task. More curves without new sectors do not answer the defeater.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: Reviewers examine a correlation-decay argument whose calculation concerns a visible sector but whose conclusion concerns the full physical spectrum.
workflows.contrast: If a proposed repair only adds more decay curves from the same incomplete observable family, the join should reject it as irrelevant to density. A narrower sectorial claim changes the conclusion honestly.

steps.title: Form the defensible claim set
steps.purpose: Recover a supported argument from the research record.
steps.input: Timeline claims; premises; counterexamples; unresolved attempts
steps.procedure: The native projection is unresolved. The argument architect selects the smallest supported contribution; failure interpretation extracts the defeated idea, learned obstruction and surviving statement.
steps.criterion: The paper mode must follow the evidence rather than the ambition of the original target.
steps.output: Intended claim ledger: conditional theorem; refuted generalization
steps.failure_next: Paper assessment consumes this bounded ledger; the native boundary supplies no automatic drafting algorithm.
steps.example: Preserve the conditional spectral estimate, report cycles as the obstruction to uniformity, and explain why the unrestricted claim was abandoned.

steps.title: Check presentation readiness
steps.purpose: Check that manuscript organization preserves claim scope.
steps.procedure: Compare proposed manuscript claims with the premises and failure record, locating any omitted assumption or contradictory status.
steps.criterion: A claim-ledger reference is insufficient unless its content faithfully represents the record.
steps.output: Paper disposition: readiness or specified claim-boundary failure
steps.failure_next: Original policy accepts readiness or stops; native return is not publication.
steps.example: A draft asserting uniform decay for all connected graphs fails because it removes the very common-gap premise challenged by the cycle example.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: A diffusion timeline contains a conditional decay derivation, a failed uniform generalization and a cycle-graph counterexample to a common spectral gap.
workflows.contrast: Removing the counterexample from the narrative while retaining the broad claim breaks fidelity to the record. Restoring the failed premise and scoped conditional theorem repairs the claim boundary without creating new evidence.

steps.title: Prepare the continuum-boundary audit
steps.purpose: Bind the representation to its physical claim boundary.
steps.input: Target context; representation proposal; continuum boundary
steps.procedure: The native preparation is unresolved. Linked procedures specify carriers, observable maps, state transport, positivity, limit order and observable completeness as separate burdens.
steps.criterion: Finite or sectorial evidence must remain distinguished from same-theory continuum and full-spectrum claims.
steps.output: Intended audit input: target identity; boundary; candidate reference
steps.failure_next: Overlay assessment consumes it; query and persistence effects in original policy are not native occurrences.
steps.example: Record decay for the visible observable family and mark density of its generated physical sector as an unproved assumption.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Test the global inference
steps.purpose: Identify unsupported physical extrapolation.
steps.procedure: Seek a sector invisible to the chosen observables and inspect whether the proposed transfer preserves the required structure.
steps.criterion: Unchanged visible correlations cannot exclude low energies in an unobserved sector.
steps.output: Overlay disposition: limited claim or quarantined global inference
steps.failure_next: Native output returns an overlay disposition; accepted status is not a continuum existence or mass-gap theorem.
steps.example: In an abstract spectral calibration, adjoin an orthogonal sector with positive energies approaching zero. Visible decay is unchanged; this exposes the missing density inference without constructing a Yang--Mills counterexample.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: A selected observable shows exponential decay, while the proposed global spectral conclusion has no proof that the observable-generated sector is dense.
workflows.contrast: If density and the required uniform extension estimates were independently established, the hidden-sector objection would need reassessment. Their mere appearance as named fields in an audit packet does not establish them.

steps.title: Identify the programme
steps.purpose: Separate the scientific target from its support.
steps.procedure: The native scope producer is unresolved. Target-freezing instructions distinguish existence, spectral exclusion, clustering, confinement and area law before selecting a programme.
steps.criterion: Different endpoints require different premises and cannot be merged by a shared label.
steps.output: Intended activation: pure-gauge programme; separate target burdens
steps.failure_next: Intake calibration consumes the activation; its existence does not establish any target theorem.
steps.example: Split the announcement into finite-observable decay, observable completeness, continuum existence, reconstruction and spectral exclusion instead of accepting one as all the others.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Judge whether inquiry can begin
steps.purpose: Assess whether the scoped question is usable.
steps.procedure: Assess whether the target and its boundaries are definite enough to investigate, retaining missing claims as obligations.
steps.criterion: Readiness concerns a usable question, not support for its ultimate conclusion.
steps.output: Intake disposition: ready, blocked or stalled
steps.failure_next: Original policy routes ready intake to grounding; the native return constructs no grounding request.
steps.example: Proceed only with the separate obligations visible; an unspecified meaning of mass gap requires target clarification before scientific grounding.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: A proposed Yang--Mills programme claims that decay of finitely many Wilson-loop observables establishes the full mass gap.
workflows.contrast: If intake is instead asked only for a finite-regulator observable estimate, continuum reconstruction is not part of that narrower result. The activation must preserve the selected target rather than silently exchanging the two questions.

steps.purpose: Ground a bounded implication problem in sources.
steps.input: Grounding request: domain; target; source references
steps.procedure: The native producer is unresolved. Linked instructions freeze theory, gauge group, quantifiers and endpoint, then bind imported claims to locatable sources with their conventions.
steps.criterion: Do not assume the desired physical scale or erase a source theorem's regulator regime.
steps.output: Intended grounding: fixed-spacing support; explicit claim ceiling

steps.title: Assess grounding adequacy

workflows.contrast: A source theorem uniform in the required limits would change the grounding burden, but only after its assumptions and theory identity were checked. Matching terminology is never sufficient transfer evidence.

steps.title: Build a discriminating frontier
steps.purpose: Expose the missing implication through representation questions.
steps.procedure: The native producer is unresolved. Linked methods compare regulators, observable coverage and representation maps, then use restricted massive, massless and hidden-sector cases to test false positives.

steps.output: Intended frontier: observable-density obligation or sectorial conclusion

steps.title: Judge frontier readiness
steps.purpose: Assess whether the frontier supports bounded derivation.
steps.input: Frontier; preserved domain and claim ceiling
steps.procedure: Check whether the chosen representation names the objects, required map and missing theorem that derivation must address.
steps.criterion: A promising representation without its transfer obligation is not an unconditional route.
steps.output: Frontier disposition: ready or quarantined
steps.failure_next: The native return is a disposition, not the frontier needed by the next workflow.
steps.example: A precise density obligation can enter derivation as an open task; a claim that visible decay already proves global exclusion must be quarantined.

workflows.case: In an abstract spectral calibration model, a visible gapped sector yields decaying correlations while an unobserved gapless sector coexists with it. This tests an inference, not existence of a gapless Yang--Mills theory. The frontier must expose the missing completeness burden.
workflows.contrast: Once the observable-generated physical subspace is known to be dense and the extension estimates are justified, the next frontier can move to remaining transfer and limit obligations. Repeating the same visible-sector fit does not supply density.

steps.title: Construct the conditional derivation
steps.purpose: Specify the mechanism’s required inequality and assumptions.
steps.procedure: The native producer is unresolved. Linked domination methods specify exposure history, retained boundary information and normalized conditional bounds; finite diagnostics attack the required implication.
steps.criterion: Joint moments cannot replace history-uniform bounds; normalization and positive-probability conditioning must be justified.
steps.output: Intended derivation packet: failed inference; open replacement obligation
steps.failure_next: Readiness assesses the packet; the declared projection is not a proof-producing algorithm.
steps.example: For P(10)=P(01)=1/2, the two-site intersection probability is zero, but P(X2=1 given X1=0)=1. Thus the suggested conditional ceiling does not follow.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

steps.title: Assess readiness for audit
steps.purpose: Assess whether the derivation is auditable.
steps.procedure: Check that the proposed inequality, retained state, assumptions and failure cases remain explicit rather than hidden by a certificate label.
steps.criterion: A finite check cannot discharge full-measure, repeated-iteration or continuum hypotheses.
steps.output: Derivation disposition: ready for scoped audit or quarantined
steps.failure_next: Original policy sends accepted packets to audit; native return omits the packet adapter.
steps.example: Send the counterexample and the requirement for a normalized history-uniform bound to audit; withhold any domination conclusion inferred only from the zero intersection moment.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: A proposed domination argument treats a small joint event probability as a history-uniform conditional ceiling. Test the finite law assigning probability one half each to outcomes 10 and 01.
workflows.contrast: A proved normalized conditional bound for every admissible positive-probability exposure history would answer this particular objection. Small unconditional intersection moments alone do not, and even that bound would not settle continuum reconstruction.

steps.title: Attack the complete implication
steps.purpose: Locate the calculation-to-endpoint inference gap.
steps.procedure: Expand volume, cutoff, distance and observable quantifiers; test hidden sectors, limit interchanges and definitions that encode the desired conclusion.
steps.criterion: A defect must target a particular inference; bounded non-refutation is not full proof.
steps.output: Refutation assessment: missing density implication or another scoped defeater
steps.failure_next: Calibration receives this assessment with the original derivation; the name independent proves no empirical independence.
steps.example: As an abstract spectral countermodel, adjoin an orthogonal sector with positive energies approaching zero, invisible to all tested observables. Their decay survives, so the general global-gap inference fails; this does not construct a Yang--Mills counterexample.

steps.title: Retain the defensible claim
steps.purpose: Calibrate the claim while preserving its valid part.
steps.procedure: Compare the audited scope with the failure, identify the strongest retained statement and state the required downgrade.
steps.criterion: Do not confuse refuting an overstrong extension with refuting its narrower conditional calculation.
steps.output: Audit disposition: retained sectorial support; quarantined full-spectrum inference
steps.failure_next: Release requires a separate audit packet preserving this content; native disposition alone is insufficient.
steps.example: Keep the visible-sector decay statement and make density an explicit missing bridge, preventing a favorable local audit from certifying a global mass gap.
steps.posture: declaration + prescribed procedure; illustration not execution

workflows.case: A conditional spectral argument relies on decay for finitely many observables and leaves density of their generated physical sector unproved.
workflows.contrast: If the packet states only visible-sector decay, the hidden-sector example does not refute that restricted calculation. It defeats the stronger global inference, so calibration must preserve the distinction.
